outcome: Global DNA methylation in hematopoietic stem cells
cohort: 64 healthy, singleton, newborn infants born at term
finding: The study suggests that mode of delivery affects the epigenetic state of neonatal hematopoietic stem cells, with infants delivered by cesarean section having globally more DNA methylated CD34+ cells than those delivered vaginally.
mod_finding: The study found that infants delivered by cesarean section had a higher degree of DNA methylation in hematopoietic stem cells compared to those delivered vaginally, potentially influencing long-term health.
